summary.intent: Plan and execute Phase 69 of CipherBox (port node/v3 model to the Rust FUSE/WinFsp desktop stack, making clients grant-root-aware) via the GSD plan-phase/execute-phase workflow, running largely unattended/auto with pre-authorized advancement from planning into execution.
summary.outcome: 16/18 plans merged with a fully green workspace: the entire crates/core+crates/sdk node/v3 foundation, the atomic FUSE cutover (69-09) and JournalOp reshape (69-18), and the grant-scope-gated delete/rename hardening (69-13) all landed after three rounds of in-execution architectural discovery and re-scoping; only 69-14 (WinFsp/Windows, requires the user's Windows machine) and a re-scoped 69-10 (legacy type cleanup) remain, and the desktop-e2e safety gate was deferred pending a separate root-key-recovery wiring effort.

repo: GSD's git-commit helper reports 'commit_failed' as a false negative even when the commit lands cleanly — always verify via `git log --oneline -1`, never retry.
gsd-executor worktree agents sometimes mis-report `expected_base` as their own last docs commit instead of the true fork point — verify via `git merge-base <branch> HEAD` before recording/merging.
Fresh worktrees lack node_modules, so husky/lint-staged pre-commit hooks fail on the first commit; `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` fixes it, or `--no-verify` is acceptable for pure-Rust commits.
cargo fmt run at the crate root (via `rustfmt lib.rs`) tends to reformat unrelated pre-existing-drift files; executors must scope-check diffs and revert stray reformatting before committing.
Claude Code's `isolation='worktree'` composes cleanly with GSD's own worktree manifest protocol (`worktree.record-agent`/`worktree.cleanup-wave`) — no conflict between the two layers.

`crates/fuse` is a read-WRITE vault owner (signs IPNS records, seals children under parent keys), unlike the TS web Phase 68.2 read-only client — any node/v3 read-adapter design that omits a write-key plane will hit an architectural wall at the FUSE consumption stage.

`ResolvedChild`/`list_folder` in crates/sdk/src/listing.rs is deliberately keyless — `resolve_child` unseals then immediately zeroizes the child read-key and never touches the write-body, so it cannot serve a write-capable consumer without an additional owned-materialization API.

`crates/sdk/src/queue.rs`'s `JournalOp` never had the `parent_metadata: FolderMetadata` field the original research cited — that weld was stale/nonexistent; always re-verify grep-line-number claims in research docs against current tree state before treating them as fact.

`RotationHighWater<S>` is not `Clone` by default; deriving Clone is safe since its `JsonSidecarFloorStore` only holds a PathBuf doing read-modify-write on disk (clones share the same durable floor, no state divergence).

Legacy `FilePointer`/`FolderMetadata`/`FileMetadata` types are NOT fully dead after the node/v3 cutover — they remain load-bearing in the recycle-bin subsystem and vault-export/restore blobs (ECIES-under-user-key, not node-to-node hops), so a blanket 'delete legacy types' plan must be re-scoped.

`publish_file_metadata` must be kept even after node/v3 migration because the Windows FUSE path (`platform/windows/operations.rs`) still calls it directly — a new `publish_file_node` was added alongside it rather than replacing it.

Desktop root read/write keys are currently placeholder-bridged from the legacy `root_folder_key` (apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/fuse/mod.rs:186) — real node/v3 root-key recovery into `KeyState` is an unwired phase-63-class stub, meaning desktop-e2e cannot exercise a real node/v3 vault yet.

`rotate_read_on_scope_exit` (grant-gated delete/rename) fails closed by design: no production `RotationDeps` implementor exists anywhere in the workspace yet (only `FakeDeps` in tests), so shared-scope-exit deletes/moves on Unix currently return EIO — a known ROT-07 live-wiring gap, not a regression.

code.finding: JournalOp::{UploadFile,MkdirPublish} originally carried only hex-string ECIES-under-user-key fields (wrapped_key_hex, parent_ipns_key_hex, etc.); 69-18 reshaped these to child_published_node/parent_child_ref/parent_write_child_ref (node/v3, D-07 dual-keyed).

InodeKind::{Root,Folder,File} were reshaped in Slice 1 to non-Option read_key/write_key/ipns_private_key (Zeroizing types), dropping legacy fields like encrypted_folder_key, file_meta_ipns_name, versions.

list_folder_owned added (69-17) as the gated write-plane tree-materialization entrypoint recovering per-node {read_key, write_key, ipns_private_key}, reusing the same pub(crate) resolve_published_node gate as list_folder (SC#6 preserved).
Comment documents that desktop bridges from the legacy root_folder_key until real node/v3 root-key recovery into KeyState is wired — a known runtime-integration gap blocking desktop-e2e.

fetch_and_decrypt_content_async migrated off ECIES to symmetric unseal_node of the file node's read_sealed body; new publish_file_node added alongside (not replacing) publish_file_metadata for first-publish + CAS-update of file content.

workflow: When an atomic/all-or-nothing plan is too large for one executor session, chunk it into bounded 'slices' on the same git branch with per-slice commits and a durable, committed runbook capturing the frozen target shape and carry-forward facts — this let the grind survive multiple session/usage-limit deaths without losing progress.

When a sub-agent reports an architectural blocker, independently re-verify its key evidentiary claims (grep counts, LOC, specific field absences) against the live tree before accepting or escalating to the user — this caught that some 'blockers' were real while distinguishing them from over-cautious halts.

For unverifiable-by-compile crypto/correctness work, prefer gating merge decisions on a live E2E run rather than compile-green alone, and be willing to surface to the user when the chosen gate becomes structurally unreachable (e.g., desktop-e2e blocked by an unrelated stub) rather than silently downgrading the safety bar.

Don't blindly rewrite hundreds of legacy-model unit tests when the model itself was deleted — deleting tests for a removed model and relying on a live E2E gate for crypto correctness avoids false-green risk, but should be flagged to the user as a strategy choice.
Re-ordering plan execution (running 69-13 before 69-10) based on discovered true dependencies rather than the original wave-numbering avoided compounding a stale plan's incorrect premise.

friction: gsd-planner crashed mid-run (API error) after writing 13 of 14 plans, requiring filesystem-fallback recovery and a fresh single-plan planner spawn.

Multiple gsd-executor worktree agents died mid-task from API errors ('response stalled mid-stream') or hit account session/usage limits, requiring manual resume/re-dispatch and careful worktree-state inspection each time.

Three successive in-execution architectural discoveries on the FUSE cutover (69-09) each required pausing execution, verifying the sub-agent's claims independently, presenting the user a decision, then spawning new research+planning rounds — turning what was scoped as a single plan into 18 total plans across multiple re-scopes.
The GSD commit helper's persistent false-negative ('commit_failed' when the commit actually succeeded) required manual git-log verification after nearly every commit throughout the session.
Executors repeatedly mis-reported their worktree's true fork base, requiring manual `git merge-base` verification before every merge to avoid a bad merge.
cargo fmt run at crate root repeatedly reformatted unrelated pre-existing-drift files, requiring scope-checks and reverts on nearly every executor run.

Slice 5's actual remaining scope was significantly underestimated by the runbook (assumed 'mechanical field-repointing' at ~35 residual errors, actual test-compile surface was ~250+ errors plus a full refresh-pipeline redesign), costing an extra grind session to re-scope.
open_items: 69-14 (WinFsp/Windows integration + TEST-03, autonomous:false) still needs to be executed on the user's Windows machine — explicit hand-off point.

69-10 ('delete legacy core types') needs re-scoping since legacy FilePointer/FolderMetadata/FileMetadata types are still legitimately used by the recycle-bin subsystem and vault-export/restore blobs and must NOT all be deleted.

Desktop-e2e verification remains deferred until desktop root-key recovery into KeyState is wired (a separate runtime-integration effort, mirroring the deferred web v2.0 stub) — treated as a known limitation, not blocking this merge, per user decision.
rotate_read_on_scope_exit (shared-scope-exit grant gate in 69-13) fails closed with EIO because no production RotationDeps implementor exists yet — the ROT-07 live-wiring gap needs a follow-up plan.
File versions are not reconstructed on write (InodeKind dropped the versions field) — a documented versioning regression to verify/fix once E2E is runnable.
Orphaned parent-CID pins are no longer unpinned after republish since metadata_cache dropped CID payload tracking — GC-able but noted as a follow-up.
SC#6 CI grep gate allowlist (bin subsystem + 69-13 reencrypt sites) should be reviewed/hardened once the desktop root-key recovery work lands.
